# trader-timemachine

The Time Machine sits between the plan and the money. trader-exit has set
the entry, the stop and the target. Before anything is sized or sent, this
skill asks one question: if today plays out like the stock's own last 60
days, how often does this plan hit the target first, the stop first, or
neither? It answers with 10,000 replays and with the real record of the same
rule on every past session. It is a simulation built from the stock's own
recent bars, not a prediction. Day trading loses most people money, and a
good-looking replay does not change that.

`${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` below is this skill's folder (where this SKILL.md lives).

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/timemachine.py" run                    # trader/plan.json, 10,000 replays, seed 19
python3 "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/timemachine.py" run --write            # also save trader/timemachine.json
python3 "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/timemachine.py" run --until 15:55      # end each replay at your flat-by time
python3 "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/timemachine.py" run --json
python3 "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/timemachine.py" run --symbol TSLA --date 2026-10-19 \
    --entry 364.18 --stop 358.32 --target 370.04 --entry-time "10:15 AM"
python3 "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/timemachine.py" chart --from           # ASCII fan chart of the saved run
```

Other flags: `--replays N`, `--seed N` (default 19), `--window N` (default 2
bars), `--offline FILE` (a saved Yahoo chart JSON, `.json` or `.json.gz`),
`--now "2026-10-19 10:15"` (New York time) to pin the clock.

## What it reads and writes

| file | what |
| --- | --- |
| `trader/plan.json` | the plan from trader-exit: symbol, date, entry, entry_time / entry_bar, stop, stop_rule, target, target_r, opening range |
| Yahoo chart API | one request: 60 days of 5-minute bars (`range=60d&interval=5m`), free and unofficial, can lag |
| `trader/timemachine.json` | with `--write`: `{plan, mc, history}` plus the verdict. `mc` holds the odds, percentiles, the fan-chart bands, 160 sample paths and a 24-bin histogram of the close |

## How it works

1. **The pool.** It keeps only FULL sessions before the plan's date: all 78
   five-minute bars, 9:30 to 4:00 New York time. Half days, gaps and today
   are left out. Every bar becomes four ratios to the bar before it:
   open, high, low and close over the previous close.
2. **One replay.** Start at the entry price. For each bar left in the day,
   pick a past bar from the same time of day (plus or minus 2 bars) at
   random, and scale it to the current price. Bar by bar, it checks the stop
   first, then the target. A bar that touches both counts as the stop.
3. **10,000 replays** give four odds. Target first. Stop first. Neither,
   which means the trade was still open at `--until` (default 4:00 PM, the
   close, or 1:00 PM on an NYSE early-close day). Green, which means target
   first or above the entry at `--until`.
   R is +1 at a 1R target, -1 at the stop, and otherwise the distance from
   the entry at `--until` divided by the risk. A gap through the stop still
   counts as -1R here. A real fill can be worse.
4. **The history.** The plan's own rule (the same opening range, stop rule
   and target R) runs again on every one of those past sessions. That is
   what really happened, not a simulation.
5. **The verdict** is one line from the numbers. It looks only at the
   replays that hit one side, and asks how often the target came first. A
   bigger target needs to win less often to break even: 1 in (1 + R). That
   is 50 % at 1R, 33 % at 2R, 25 % at 3R. Less than 5 points from break-even:
   "Close to a coin flip" at 1R, "Close to break-even" at any other R. 5 to
   15 points: "Leans toward the target" or "Leans toward the stop". 15 or
   more: "Strongly toward" one of them. So a 2R plan with target first
   24.1 % and stop first 50.5 % is close to break-even (it needs 33 % of
   the 74.6 % that hit a side, and got 32 %), not a loser.
6. **Below the verdict**, when it applies: a line when more than 40 % of the
   replays hit neither (the price at `--until` decides those), and the
   average R when its sign goes against the lean. Those can only point the
   other way because of the replays that hit neither.

**The seed.** The draws come from Python's `random.Random(seed)`, seed 19 by
default. Same plan, same data, same seed: the same numbers, on any machine.
Say the seed with every result so the user can repeat it.

**5-minute bars only.** Yahoo keeps 60 days of 5-min bars but only about 7
days of 1-min bars, too few sessions for a fair pool. It refuses, in one
plain line, when there are fewer than 20 full sessions, when the entry bar is
not in the data (wrong date, not closed yet, a future day), or when the plan
does not make sense (a stop above a buy's entry, an entry off the 5-minute
grid). A live in-progress bar is never used.

## Steps

1. Make sure `trader/plan.json` is today's plan from `/trader-exit`. If there
   is none, run that first, or pass the plan as flags.
2. Run `timemachine.py run --write`. Add `--until 15:55` when the plan has a
   flat-by time, so "neither" means still open at the time you would get out.
3. Tell the user, in this order: the four odds, the median and the 5 to 95
   range of the price at the close, the average R, the history line, then the
   verdict line and any line under it exactly as printed. Say the seed.
4. If the verdict is a coin flip or close to break-even, say so plainly. Do
   not dress it up. If the history and the replays disagree, say that too.
5. Say once that this is built from the last 60 days and is not a prediction.
   Earnings, news and halts can do things those 60 days never did. Check
   `/trader-news` for the stock before going on.
6. If the user still wants the trade, hand off to `/trader-budget` to size it.

## Example: the reel

TSLA, Monday 2026-10-19. The 15-minute opening range is 354.47 to 362.18.
The 10:10 bar closes above it: entry 364.18 at 10:15 AM (bar 8), stop 358.32
(the range midpoint, rounded down), target 370.04 (1R, risk 5.86 a share).

```
10,000 replays of the rest of the session, 10:15 AM to 4:00 PM (69 five-minute bars), seed 19.
  target first   29.4 %
  stop first     25.5 %
  neither        45.1 %   still open at 4:00 PM
  green          51.7 %   target first, or above the entry at 4:00 PM
  Price at 4:00 PM: median 364.36, 90 % of replays between 355.54 and 373.54.
  Average R: +0.034
History: the same rule on each of those 59 real sessions fired 33 times:
13 target, 15 stop, 5 neither. Average R -0.062.
Close to a coin flip: target first 29.4 % vs stop first 25.5 %.
45.1 % of the replays hit neither by 4:00 PM; the price at 4:00 PM decides those.
```

At 1R the target has to come first in half of the replays that hit one
side. It did in 53.6 %. The replays came out close to a coin flip, and the
real history was slightly worse than even. That is the honest answer for this setup, and it is what
the user should hear before `/trader-budget` sizes 8 shares.

## Rules

- Every number comes from the run. Never round a coin flip up into an edge.
- The verdict line and the lines under it are printed by the tool. Repeat
  them, do not rewrite them. Never judge a 2R or 3R plan by target first vs
  stop first alone: the verdict already weighs the target's R.
- Simulated odds are not predictions and not promises. Say it once, plainly.
- Free Yahoo data is unofficial and can lag. Bars are 5-minute bars, checked
  bar by bar, never tick by tick and never real time.
- Always say the seed, so any run can be repeated.
- One plan per run. A changed entry, stop, target or date is a new run.

## What it never does

It never places an order, never sizes a position, never changes the plan,
and never calls a result a sure thing. It never prints a P&L or a profit.
It never uses a bar that has not closed yet, and never mixes today's bars
into the pool.

- Paper by default (`"paper": true`): trader-risk blocks every order unless the Merrymen agent is in
  practice (paper) mode. Going live is the owner's own decision, made in Merrymen and in their own config.
- Nothing in this pack trades except trader-broker, and only through four gates: trader-risk passed that
  exact order today, the user typed an explicit yes for that one order in the chat, Claude's own
  permission card for propose_trade was allowed once, and the owner approved the proposal in Merrymen.
  The agent's signed limits still apply after that. Never set the Merrymen trade tools to "Always allow".
- Merrymen holds no resting stop or target order: getting out is a sell the owner approves, so it can

bars), `--offline FILE` (a saved Yahoo chart JSON, `.json` or `.json.gz`),
`--now "2026-10-19 10:15"` (New York time) to pin the clock.

## What it reads and writes

| file | what |
| --- | --- |
| `trader/plan.json` | the plan from trader-exit: symbol, date, entry, entry_time / entry_bar, stop, stop_rule, target, target_r, opening range |
| Yahoo chart API | one request: 60 days of 5-minute bars (`range=60d&interval=5m`), free and unofficial, can lag |
| `trader/timemachine.json` | with `--write`: `{plan, mc, history}` plus the verdict. `mc` holds the odds, percentiles, the fan-chart bands, 160 sample paths and a 24-bin histogram of the close |

## How it works

1. **The pool.** It keeps only FULL sessions before the plan's date: all 78
   five-minute bars, 9:30 to 4:00 New York time. Half days, gaps and today
   are left out. Every bar becomes four ratios to the bar before it:
   open, high, low and close over the previous close.
2. **One replay.** Start at the entry price. For each bar left in the day,
   pick a past bar from the same time of day (plus or minus 2 bars) at
   random, and scale it to the current price. Bar by bar, it checks the stop
   first, then the target. A bar that touches both counts as the stop.
3. **10,000 replays** give four odds. Target first. Stop first. Neither,
   which means the trade was still open at `--until` (default 4:00 PM, the
   close, or 1:00 PM on an NYSE early-close day). Green, which means target
   first or above the entry at `--until`.
   R is +1 at a 1R target, -1 at the stop, and otherwise the distance from
   the entry at `--until` divided by the risk. A gap through the stop still
   counts as -1R here. A real fill can be worse.
4. **The history.** The plan's own rule (the same opening range, stop rule
   and target R) runs again on every one of those past sessions. That is
   what really happened, not a simulation.
5. **The verdict** is one line from the numbers. It looks only at the
   replays that hit one side, and asks how often the target came first. A
   bigger target needs to win less often to break even: 1 in (1 + R). That
   is 50 % at 1R, 33 % at 2R, 25 % at 3R. Less than 5 points from break-even:
   "Close to a coin flip" at 1R, "Close to break-even" at any other R. 5 to
   15 points: "Leans toward the target" or "Leans toward the stop". 15 or
   more: "Strongly toward" one of them. So a 2R plan with target first
   24.1 % and stop first 50.5 % is close to break-even (it needs 33 % of
   the 74.6 % that hit a side, and got 32 %), not a loser.
6. **Below the verdict**, when it applies: a line when more than 40 % of the
   replays hit neither (the price at `--until` decides those), and the
   average R when its sign goes against the lean. Those can only point the
   other way because of the replays that hit neither.

**The seed.** The draws come from Python's `random.Random(seed)`, seed 19 by
default. Same plan, same data, same seed: the same numbers, on any machine.
Say the seed with every result so the user can repeat it.

**5-minute bars only.** Yahoo keeps 60 days of 5-min bars but only about 7
days of 1-min bars, too few sessions for a fair pool. It refuses, in one
plain line, when there are fewer than 20 full sessions, when the entry bar is
not in the data (wrong date, not closed yet, a future day), or when the plan
does not make sense (a stop above a buy's entry, an entry off the 5-minute
grid). A live in-progress bar is never used.

## Steps

1. Make sure `trader/plan.json` is today's plan from `/trader-exit`. If there
   is none, run that first, or pass the plan as flags.
2. Run `timemachine.py run --write`. Add `--until 15:55` when the plan has a
   flat-by time, so "neither" means still open at the time you would get out.
3. Tell the user, in this order: the four odds, the median and the 5 to 95
   range of the price at the close, the average R, the history line, then the
   verdict line and any line under it exactly as printed. Say the seed.
4. If the verdict is a coin flip or close to break-even, say so plainly. Do
   not dress it up. If the history and the replays disagree, say that too.
5. Say once that this is built from the last 60 days and is not a prediction.
   Earnings, news and halts can do things those 60 days never did. Check
   `/trader-news` for the stock before going on.
6. If the user still wants the trade, hand off to `/trader-budget` to size it.

## Example: the reel

TSLA, Monday 2026-10-19. The 15-minute opening range is 354.47 to 362.18.
The 10:10 bar closes above it: entry 364.18 at 10:15 AM (bar 8), stop 358.32
(the range midpoint, rounded down), target 370.04 (1R, risk 5.86 a share).

```
10,000 replays of the rest of the session, 10:15 AM to 4:00 PM (69 five-minute bars), seed 19.
  target first   29.4 %
  stop first     25.5 %
  neither        45.1 %   still open at 4:00 PM
  green          51.7 %   target first, or above the entry at 4:00 PM
  Price at 4:00 PM: median 364.36, 90 % of replays between 355.54 and 373.54.
  Average R: +0.034
History: the same rule on each of those 59 real sessions fired 33 times:
13 target, 15 stop, 5 neither. Average R -0.062.
Close to a coin flip: target first 29.4 % vs stop first 25.5 %.
45.1 % of the replays hit neither by 4:00 PM; the price at 4:00 PM decides those.
```

At 1R the target has to come first in half of the replays that hit one
side. It did in 53.6 %. The replays came out close to a coin flip, and the
real history was slightly worse than even. That is the honest answer for this setup, and it is what
the user should hear before `/trader-budget` sizes 8 shares.

## Rules

- Every number comes from the run. Never round a coin flip up into an edge.
- The verdict line and the lines under it are printed by the tool. Repeat
  them, do not rewrite them. Never judge a 2R or 3R plan by target first vs
  stop first alone: the verdict already weighs the target's R.
- Simulated odds are not predictions and not promises. Say it once, plainly.
- Free Yahoo data is unofficial and can lag. Bars are 5-minute bars, checked
  bar by bar, never tick by tick and never real time.
- Always say the seed, so any run can be repeated.
- One plan per run. A changed entry, stop, target or date is a new run.

## What it never does

It never places an order, never sizes a position, never changes the plan,
and never calls a result a sure thing. It never prints a P&L or a profit.
It never uses a bar that has not closed yet, and never mixes today's bars
into the pool.

## Safety

- Education and tooling, not financial advice. A PASS is a rules check, not a recommendation.
- Paper by default (`"paper": true`): trader-risk blocks every order unless the Merrymen agent is in
  practice (paper) mode. Going live is the owner's own decision, made in Merrymen and in their own config.
- Nothing in this pack trades except trader-broker, and only through four gates: trader-risk passed that
  exact order today, the user typed an explicit yes for that one order in the chat, Claude's own
  permission card for propose_trade was allowed once, and the owner approved the proposal in Merrymen.
  The agent's signed limits still apply after that. Never set the Merrymen trade tools to "Always allow".
- Merrymen holds no resting stop or target order: getting out is a sell the owner approves, so it can
  fill well past the stop. No options, margin, short selling or leverage.
- Claude never sees wallet keys, never signs, never turns on live trading and never changes a signed
  limit. Sign-in happens on Merrymen's own page, never in the chat.

skills.name: connect
skills.desc: Connect Claude Code to Merrymen, prepare a new agent with owner-reviewed setup, or fix a connection that is not working. Use when the user asks to set up or sign in to Merrymen, or when a Merrymen request finds no Merrymen tools.

---
name: connect
description: Connect Claude Code to Merrymen, prepare a new agent with owner-reviewed setup, or fix a connection that is not working. Use when the user asks to set up or sign in to Merrymen, or when a Merrymen request finds no Merrymen tools.
---

Help the owner connect this Claude Code to Merrymen.

**First check.** Look for Merrymen tools in this session (their names end in `list_agents`, `get_agent_status`, `search_tokens` and so on). Any one of them means Merrymen is connected; which ones are there shows what the owner allowed, because a tool whose permission was left unticked is not offered at all.
- None at all: go to the sign-in steps below.
- `get_merryman_setup` is there: call it first, even for a new owner. Use its reported next step; no visible agent does not prove no wallet exists. If the owner requested creation and drafting is allowed, call `create_merryman` with their name, strategy and risk choices, then show its owner review link. The owner reviews the exact setup and continues to wallet creation and trading-permission signing in Merrymen. Read setup again after signing; a draft or approval is not a running agent.
- Only `list_agents` is there: call it and report which agents are shared; use `/merrymen:status` or `/merrymen:why` for an existing agent. Do not infer that an empty result authorizes replacing a wallet.
- Some Merrymen tools but no `list_agents`: say it is connected but cannot see their agent (it was made without "See your agent's status and settings"), and list what it can do from the tools that are there.
- If the owner came here because a request needed a tool that is not there, name the permission it needs: `get_agent_status` needs "See your agent's status and settings", `explain_agent_inactivity` "See your agent's decisions", `get_portfolio` "See your portfolio and trades", `get_summary` "Create reports and exports", `search_tokens` "Research markets and public agents". They add a permission by signing in again (step 1 below) and ticking it under "Change what … can do"; a reconnect keeps what they allowed before.

For an existing agent, use `create_agent_draft` or `propose_settings_change` for requested configuration changes and return the owner review link. Never use new-agent creation to replace an existing agent. After activation, Merrymen's hosted worker runs independently of this conversation; no terminal or chat must stay open. Report permission expiry, service or funding blockers from the actual setup response.

Hosts with MCP Apps can show the interactive Merryman home for naming, strategy, risk, status, portfolio, activity, settings and alerts. Claude Code can use the same text responses and tools; an embedded view is optional. Other research, trade proposals, reports and community actions stay available in chat when their permission is granted.

If the requested work is complete, stop there; reconnect only when access is missing.

**Otherwise, tell the owner how to sign in.** You cannot do this step for them: it happens in their browser, on Merrymen's own page.

1. Type `/mcp`, choose **plugin:merrymen:merrymen**, and choose **Authenticate**. (From a terminal instead: `claude mcp login plugin:merrymen:merrymen`.) With this plugin installed, this is the entry to sign in to even if they already added Merrymen to Claude on claude.ai: the plugin's server takes the place of that connector.
2. Merrymen opens in the browser. Sign in if asked, check what Claude Code will be able to do, and click **Allow**.
3. Come back and call `get_merryman_setup`, or run `/merrymen:status` for an existing agent.

More ways to connect, for other assistants: https://app.merrymen.dev/connect/mcp.

**What the connection can and cannot do.** It sees only the agent and the permissions the owner allows on that page, and they can disconnect it at any time on Connected apps (https://app.merrymen.dev/connect/apps). With the usual permissions it can also message the agent, run backtests and manage the watchlist and alerts. It can suggest trades or setting changes only if the owner allowed that, and nothing happens until they approve each one in Merrymen. It can never move their funds, see their keys, turn on live trading or loosen their limits.

name: token
description: Research a token for the user's Merrymen agent — look it up by address or symbol, read its market data and check whether the agent could buy it. Use when the user asks about a token in the context of Merrymen.
argument-hint: "<token address or symbol>"
---

Research the token "$ARGUMENTS" with the Merrymen tools (their names end in `search_tokens`, `get_token` and `check_token_eligibility`).

1. If "$ARGUMENTS" is empty, ask which token (an address is best).
2. Call `search_tokens` with it. If several tokens share the symbol, list them by address and ask which one; symbols can be copied or impersonated.
3. For the chosen address, call `get_token`, and, if the owner has an agent, `check_token_eligibility`.
4. Keep three things apart: whether the token can be found, whether it has a price, and whether the agent could buy it. Cite each figure's source and time.
5. When you say whether the agent could buy it, say which book that is from `check_token_eligibility`'s `book`: paper buys are simulated, live buys use real funds. "Could buy" is about buying; selling a token the agent already holds needs only its permission's sell coverage.
